parse.description: Read a log of OpenROAD and give typed records, without a tool run. Inputs: log (the log, relative to the design root), liberty (optional; a list of Liberty files: the report gives the library name and nominal conditions of each). Measurements: errors, warnings; for each repair table n of repair_timing or repair_design: repair<n>_rows, repair<n>_wns_ns, repair<n>_tns_ns, repair<n>_buffers (the last row); route_usage_pct (over all routing resources of the die), route_overflow, route_wirelength_um. Diagnostics: one error per error message code; one warning per repair table that shows a known pattern: buffer_limit (the repair stopped at the maximum buffer count), one_pass_per_endpoint (a hold repair that made one sweep), worst_slack_constant, margin_only (all checks met; the message is about the margin). Use it when a repair step says 'unable to repair', before you name a cause.

timing.description: Check the log or report of a timing step (OpenSTA, or OpenROAD with report_checks, report_wns, report_tns, report_worst_slack, report_check_types), without a tool run. Inputs: log (relative to the design root), clock_period_ns (optional; default: the -period of a create_clock line of the log for the clock of the worst path (a line of another clock is not used), else the two clock edge rows of that path when they are the same edge of one clock), time_unit (optional: fs, ps, ns, us, ms or s; default: the unit that the log states with report_units or set_cmd_units, else ns as an assumption), max_slack_periods (optional, default 10), max_violations (optional, default 0). The check is 'not run' when the log has no complete slack line and no wns, tns or worst slack line (a path header without its slack line is not a result; an exit code 0 of the script does not show this), and when a line after the last result says that the tool had no design (a failed run appended to an old log). It is 'invalid check' when the worst slack is more than max_slack_periods clock periods negative, or when more than max_violations max slew, max fanout or max capacitance violations remain in the newest report after the last repair (for example a check before the placement where repair_design inserted no buffer). Else it is 'valid'. The slack limit is not checked (measurement slack_limit_check is missing, with the reason 'not run') when the slack is negative and the period is not known, or when clock_period_ns is given and the log does not state its time unit: give time_unit. Measurements: timing_check (1 when valid; else failed with the reason), worst_slack_ns (measured only when valid; the lowest slack line or worst slack line), wns_ns, slack_limit_check, paths, slack_lines, worst_path_stages, worst_path_logic_depth (the data path, without cells of the clock network), clock_period_ns, repair_buffers, max_slew_violations, max_fanout_violations, max_capacitance_violations. The response status is failed for 'not run' and 'invalid check'. The report of an invalid check has no slack value. Use it before you report a slack from a script or a hand-made timing run. For an invalid check before the placement, report the stages and the logic depth of the worst path, not the slack.

spef.description: Check an extracted SPEF file for wire resistance, without a tool run. Inputs: spef (relative to the design root; .gz is read), max_zero_fraction (optional, default 0.25: the share of the resistance segments that can be 0 ohm). A resistance is one number or a triplet (best:typical:worst); each is one segment, and the segments of 0 ohm are counted for each of the three corners. The check is 'invalid' when the file has no net, a missing or unknown *R_UNIT or *C_UNIT, a row of a *RES section that is not a resistance, no resistance segment, a negative segment, only segments of 0 ohm, or more segments of 0 ohm than max_zero_fraction; else 'valid'. A file that cannot be read (for example a .gz file that is not gzip data) gives 'not run'. Measurements: spef_check (1 when valid; else failed with the reason, or missing when the check did not run), nets, res_segments, res_zero_segments, res_negative_segments, res_bad_rows, res_zero_fraction, res_total_ohm (the typical values), cap_total_pf. The response status is failed for an invalid file and for a check that did not run. Use it before you report timing with extracted wires: an extraction can end without an error and write no wire resistance (for example extract_parasitics -lef_res with a technology LEF without RESISTANCE values).
